title: Complementing unambiguous partially blind counter languages
formal: For every unambiguous one-way partially blind multicounter machine M, does some nondeterministic one-way partially blind multicounter machine N satisfy \(L(N)=\Sigma^*\setminus L(M)\) over the same input alphabet?
definitions: A machine has finite control and finitely many nonnegative integer counters, initially zero. A step consumes the next input letter, consumes the right endmarker, or is an epsilon step consuming nothing. It inspects one selected counter with guard zero, positive, or no guard, then changes that counter by −1, 0 or +1 and changes state. A decrement requires the positive guard. Input is read once from left to right; after the endmarker only epsilon steps are possible. A finite run accepts after consuming the entire input and endmarker if its state is final and all counters are zero. It need not be a maximal run. For a partially blind machine, zero guards are forbidden; positive guards and unguarded transitions remain allowed. A blocked decrement yields no successor, with no zero-detection alternative. Unambiguous means each input has at most one accepting finite transition sequence, including epsilon steps; nonaccepting branches may be numerous or infinite. The output machine N need not be unambiguous. It may have a different finite number of counters, but has the same nonnegativity, endmarker and final-zero acceptance conventions. No counter magnitude, reversal or runtime bound is imposed. Complement includes the empty word when appropriate. The question asks existence of N and does not add an effective or size-efficient translation requirement.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked closure theorem into the nondeterministic partially blind class, or an unambiguous source machine whose complement is proved outside that entire class. Showing only that the complement is not deterministic or not unambiguous is insufficient.
context: The source asks whether its complement result for deterministic finite-testable machines extends to unambiguous machines. Unambiguity constrains accepting runs while still allowing many unsuccessful branches.
why: This isolates the interaction between unambiguity, weak counters and negation.

import_provenance.original_title: Complementing unambiguous partially blind counter languages
import_provenance.original_statement: Is the complement of every language accepted by an unambiguous one-way partially blind multicounter machine accepted by some nondeterministic partially blind multicounter machine? Equivalently, ask this for unambiguous finite-testable multicounter machines; the output machine need not remain unambiguous.

sentences: Partially blind counters cannot branch on a successful zero test.
Acceptance still requires all counters to be zero at the end.
The source machine has at most one accepting run per input.
Its complement is allowed an arbitrary nondeterministic machine of the same counter type.
The target therefore does not demand preservation of unambiguity.
